newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders can't confirm China soybean talk.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders can't confirm China soybean talk.

text.p: Brazilian traders could not confirm talk that China was back in the market for South American soybeans and soymeal, although they thought further sales were possible.
"We don't know anything about it," said Michael McDougall, director of commodities futures at Fimat Futures. "It's possible they could come into the market."
Traders in the U.S. and Argentina reported China was making enquiries into soybeans and soyproducts following a drop in prices on the Chicago commodities futures exchange Wednesday.
But some traders said Chinese interest was continuing.
"There has been a certain amount of activity recently," said one trader, although he would specify neither a timeframe nor quantities sold.
Demand might also taper off following the price drop, which means the differential between Brazil and the U.S. is becoming less attractive, McDougall said.
"The prices were conducive but with the market falling like it has, it's starting to look less probable," he said.
